clue.text: Didn't succeed in crossing the ice?

definitions.meaning: a plan that collapsed or came to nothing
playfully, someone crossing thin ice who drops into the water below

explanation.surface: A skater's failed attempt to get across a frozen pond.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second, literal reading: a skater who breaks the ice and plunges in.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a deal or plan that collapsed is said to have dropped through, never coming to fruition.

clue.text: Having broken rib, feel delirious

indicators.note: something broken is smashed into pieces, so the letters of the next words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient with a fractured rib feels light-headed and confused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' looks like part of the injury but tells you to shuffle RIB and FEEL together.
explanation.definitionFit: Near synonym: a feverish, overexcited state, as when a high temperature makes a patient wander in mind.

clue.text: Three animals in the lead

definitions.meaning: a hunting term for a set of three hounds, hares or similar creatures
the strap by which a dog is walked

explanation.surface: Three animals out in front of a group or race.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a dog's restraining strap and an old sporting term for a trio of hounds or hares.

clue.text: Recorded as having been dismantled

definitions.meaning: written down in notes, as minutes are
taken apart, as a tent or scaffolding is

explanation.surface: Something noted in writing because it had been taken to pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers both writing notes and lowering or disassembling a structure.

clue.text: Note in the morning papers

definitions.note: a plural phrase for a single quantity of paper, 480 or 500 sheets

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
AM, ante meridiem, is the morning

explanation.surface: A memo slipped into the morning newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'papers' suggests newspapers, but it means a stack of writing paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of measure for sheets of paper, so a bundle of papers.

clue.text: Lacking weight, emptied the Chamber

definitions.meaning: took the cartridges out of a gun's firing chamber

explanation.surface: Parliament's chamber cleared out, leaving it without weight of numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital C makes 'Chamber' look parliamentary; it is the chamber of a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun with its cartridges removed, or a vehicle with its cargo taken off, is in this state.

clue.text: You could make a hash of onomatopoeic sounds of laughter

indicators.note: with 'of', making a hash of something is jumbling it, so the words a hash are rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning that you might bungle your attempt at imitating laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make a hash of' sounds like a botched job; here 'a hash' is the fodder to jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Laughter written as it sounds, the repeated syllable that represents someone chuckling.

clue.text: Reserve enclosure, after a fashion

indicators.note: the enclosure word is placed after the fashion word

parts.note: a mode is a fashion or style
a sty is a pen enclosing pigs

explanation.surface: A reserved enclosure, set up in some fashion or other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after a fashion' reads as 'somewhat'; split it so 'after' orders the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: reserve as a personal quality, holding back and not showing off.

clue.text: Brave pirate's superficial improvement

parts.note: to face danger is to brave it
to pirate is to steal, or lift, someone's work

explanation.surface: A bold buccaneer whose looks have been only skin-deep improved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave pirate' reads as noun phrase; both words are verbs here.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative use: a cosmetic renovation that smartens appearance without real change, like cosmetic surgery.

clue.text: Exact money?

parts.note: 'exact' as a verb, to extort, so extorting money by threats

explanation.surface: Having the right change ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exact' looks like an adjective (the correct sum) but is the verb meaning to demand.
explanation.definitionFit: Extortion: demanding payment under threat of exposure is exacting money.

clue.text: To save is difficult with nothing coming in

indicators.note: the zero goes into the middle of the word for difficult

parts.note: difficult means hard
O, a zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Saving is tough when no money comes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to stockpile and store away, like a squirrel with nuts.

clue.text: Available with deferred payment

definitions.meaning: ready for use, at one's disposal
paid in arrears, as when wages are kept back a week

explanation.surface: Something you can have now and pay for later.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means held ready, and also describes work paid for after it is done.

clue.text: He's smart to order pets

indicators.note: putting letters in order is arranging them anew, so the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clever man who buys animals made to order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He's smart' reads as praise but is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: small rodents commonly kept in cages as children's pets.

clue.text: One's in charge but sometimes has a leader

definitions.text: One's in charge but sometimes has a leader

parts.words: One's in charge but sometimes has a leader
parts.note: a newspaper's boss writes the leader, the paper's opinion column

explanation.surface: A paradox: the person in charge who nonetheless has a leader above.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' seems to be a boss; in Britain a leader is a newspaper's editorial column.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a newspaper is in charge and produces the leading article.

clue.text: Very frightened, I take a short rest before I can set off

indicators.note: the rest comes ahead of the jumbled letters

parts.note: a nap is a brief sleep

indicators.note: set off as in set going, startled into a new order, so the letters of I and can are rearranged

explanation.surface: Scared, someone grabs a quick nap before setting out on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set off' looks like departing but signals rearranging I CAN into ANIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: being in a state of sudden fear or alarm, terrified and agitated.

clue.text: Salad item — you can add it in haste

indicators.note: the word it goes into the salad vegetable

parts.note: celery is a salad vegetable

explanation.surface: A recipe tip about adding a salad vegetable when in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in haste' reads as 'hurriedly'; 'in' is the container and 'haste' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: swiftness of movement, a formal word for speed.

clue.text: Cosmetic watch-dog?

parts.note: to eye something is to watch it
to dog someone is to follow them closely, to shadow them

explanation.surface: A guard dog used as a beauty product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'watch-dog' looks like one noun; split it into two verbs, eye and shadow.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a powder or cream applied to the eyelids as make-up.

clue.text: Tightly packed Wimbledon crowd may well enjoy it

definitions.meaning: placed very near together, as eyes or houses can be

definitions.text: Wimbledon crowd may well enjoy it
definitions.meaning: a tense, evenly fought tennis set that tennis fans relish

explanation.surface: A dense Wimbledon audience enjoying the tennis.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the London tennis championship; a tight set there thrills spectators.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyphenated adjective means placed near together; read as two words it is a tightly contested tennis set.

clue.text: Provides soft soap and cloths for the cricket team?

definitions.meaning: soft soap is flattery, so this means flatters
cricketers wear white woollen trousers, so the team is named by its kit

explanation.surface: A shop supplying toiletries and towels for a cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is a verb for flattering, the plural of a washcloth, and white cricket trousers worn by the team.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers flattering talk, face cloths, and the white trousers that stand for cricketers.

clue.text: Power is off — cold inside

indicators.note: the cold letter goes inside the word for off

parts.note: something off is not working properly, faulty
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A power cut leaves the house cold indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Power is off' reads as an outage; 'Power' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an ability or capacity, as in mental powers.

clue.text: He goes to clinic initially, twitching and feverish

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of clinic

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary twitching

explanation.surface: A patient attends a clinic shaking and running a temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: frantically busy, full of agitated activity, originally also meaning fever-flushed.

clue.text: Catnaps — possibly that provides energy for the sailor

definitions.text: that provides energy for the sailor

indicators.note: possibly suggests one possible arrangement of the letters of the preceding word

explanation.surface: Short naps might be what keeps a sailor going.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: sailors push a ship's winch round to haul anchor, so it turns their effort into lifting power.
explanation.definitionFit: A revolving drum on a ship used for winding cable, converting the crew's pushing into hauling power.

clue.text: It is backed in race to be beat

indicators.note: the turned letters go into the word for race

parts.note: a chase is a race or pursuit

indicators.note: backed means the contraction is read backwards

parts.note: it is contracts to it's

explanation.surface: A racehorse is backed but beaten in the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' sounds like betting on a horse, but it is the reversal signal; 'It is' must first be contracted to IT'S, apostrophe dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to punish, especially physically, as by thrashing.

clue.text: Moon-affected, in the main

definitions.meaning: governed by the moon's pull, as the sea's rise and fall is
the main is the open sea, so relating to the ocean's ebb and flow

explanation.surface: Mostly influenced by the moon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the main' reads as 'mostly'; the main is the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebb and flow of the sea is caused by the moon, and happens in the ocean.

clue.text: Parliamentary official rising to arouse the House?

parts.note: a whip is the party official who keeps MPs in line
up means rising, as when standing up

explanation.surface: A party whip stands up to stir Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the House' looks like the Commons; the question mark hints at stirring any audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb: to stir up or excite feelings, as in rousing a crowd or audience.

clue.text: New lamps that will be put into service

definitions.text: that will be put into service

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters of the next word

explanation.surface: New lamps to be brought into use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' looks like being put to use; it is a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacred song from the Bible sung or recited in church worship.

clue.text: Follow, in the end

definitions.meaning: the rear part or last section, as of an animal or a queue

explanation.surface: Eventually someone follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the end' looks like 'eventually'; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for following secretly and a noun for the rear end.

clue.text: Landowner has to ring back about river

indicators.note: the turned letters go round the river letter
back means the word for ring is read backwards

parts.note: to ring is to dial a phone number

explanation.surface: An estate owner has to return a call about a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns DIAL into LAID; LAID goes about R. A laird is a Scottish landowner.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland, the owner of a landed estate is given this title.

clue.text: Either rise quickly or don't budge

parts.note: to stand is to rise to one's feet
fast means quickly

explanation.surface: An order offering a choice: get up fast or stay put.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Either ... or' looks like a choice of meanings; it is a charade then a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to hold firm and refuse to give ground or yield.

clue.text: Small 'w' on sign? That's novel

parts.note: little means small
an omen is a sign of things to come

explanation.surface: A lower-case w on a signboard is something new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small w' is a little W; 'novel' looks like an adjective but is the book.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Louisa May Alcott's classic 1868 novel about the four March sisters.
